newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Hirsch Servo debuts on Vienna's small-cap market.
newsitem.headline: Hirsch Servo debuts on Vienna's small-cap market.

text.p: Austrian machinery and packaging maker Hirsch Servo said on Friday it would issue 160,200 common shares in an initial offering next week, becoming the first issuer to debut on the Vienna bourse's mid-cap segment Fit.

The 140,000 new shares and 20,200 old shares, with a nominal value of 100 schillings each, represent 32 percent of the firm's equity capital. They would be priced at between 680 and 740 schillings each to raise up to 118.5 million schillings in fresh funds, Hirsch Servo said in a statement.
Investors can subscribe to the issue between June 13 and 19. The issue price will be fixed on June 12.

Hirsch Servo reported pre-tax profits of 16.8 million schillings for its 1995/96 business year on group sales of 225.7 million schillings. It expects pre-tax profits to rise to 31.5 million schillings in 1996/97 and to 42.4 million in 1997/98.
The Vienna stock exchange hopes its new Fit market will boost liquidity on what is still one of Europe's smallest markets. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
